state_background_check.value: Florida has a facially broad state constitutional disqualification, but it cannot reach a candidate for the U.S. House or Senate. Fla. Const. Art. VI, §4(a) bars anyone 'convicted of a felony' from being 'qualified to vote or hold office until restoration of civil rights or removal of disability' — text not expressly limited to state office. However, under the Qualifications Clauses (U.S. Const. Art. I, §2, cl.2 for the House; §3, cl.3 for the Senate) as construed in U.S. Term Limits, Inc. v. Thornton, 514 U.S. 779 (1995), states may not add qualifications for Congress beyond the Constitution's own age/citizenship/residency requirements, and each chamber alone judges its members' qualifications (Art. I, §5). Confirming this in practice: Florida's own 2024 Federal Qualifying Handbook (FL Division of Elections) lists only the three federal constitutional qualifications for U.S. House and Senate candidates (citizenship years, age, state inhabitancy) — no felony or background-check requirement appears anywhere in the federal candidate-qualifying chapters — and Fla. Stat. §99.012 ('Restrictions on individuals qualifying for public office') likewise contains no criminal-history provision and expressly exempts 'persons holding any federal office' from its concurrent-term resign-to-run rule. No FL statute or rule requires a background check as part of federal candidate qualifying.
state_background_check.snippet: No person convicted of a felony, or adjudicated in this or any other state to be mentally incompetent, shall be qualified to vote or hold office until restoration of civil rights or removal of disability.

employment_record.snippet: As a 7th Grade Civics Teacher at Lincoln Middle School in Gainesville, Florida, Seth Harp is teaching the next generation of Americans about government, citizenship, civic responsibility and the power of democracy. Every day, he works to help young people understand not only how our government functions but also how they can become active participants in shaping its future.​ Seth s involvement in politics began long before he was old enough to cast a ballot. During the 1990s, he volunteered on Election Days, helping arrange transportation to polling locations for voters who otherwise may not have had a way to make their voices heard. Those early experiences instilled in him a lifelong belief that democracy works best when everyone has the opportunity to participate. ​After graduating from college, Seth became one of the youngest talk show hosts in the history of WKZO Radio in Kalamazoo, Michigan at just 23 years old. The station s rich history included broadcasting legends such as Paul Harvey, Harry Caray and Tom Snyder. That opportunity launched a media career spanning more than 25 years.​ Over the course of his career, Seth served as a Program Director, Operations Manager, Station Manager, and on-air host across six states. Since 2001, he has managed and operated nine radio stations and media organizations, helping develop and mentor countless broadcasters, journalists, and media professional who have gone on to successful careers at ESPN, FOX Sports, CBS, and other major media companies across the country.​ After moving to Florida more than a decade ago, Seth found not only a home, but a community worth fighting for. As Operations Manager of ESPN Gainesville and later as an Adjunct Professor in the University of Florida s College of Journalism and Communications, Seth helped train and mentor future communicators, broadcasters, and media leaders.

bio_summary.value: A fifth-generation Floridian raised in Gainesville in the 1970s, Mike’s childhood was all sun-scorched summers at Crescent Beach, Camp Crystal Lake, horse riding near Kanapaha, fantastic music, barbeque sandwiches at Chiapini’s, and long afternoons tubing the Ichetucknee. No rules, no shoes, no reason to believe that society would ever feel this disconnected.
